question: Select the correct combination of novelist and their works.
solution:
The correct answer is__** Jhootha Sach – Yashpal**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jhootha Sach – Yashpal**

 
 
• **​This pair is ***Correct.*
 
• *Jhootha Sach* (translated as *False Truth*) is indeed written by **Yashpal**.
 
• This novel is o**ne of the important works in Hindi literature,**
 
• It r**eflects the struggle of people during the Indian independence movemen**t and the post-independence period.
 
• The novel explores the disillusionment that people faced in the post-independence period in India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tamas – Shrilal Shukla**

 
 
• This is **incorrect**.
 
• The novel *Tamas* was written by **Bhisham Sahani**, not Shrilal Shukla.
 
• *Tamas* is a** powerful novel that portrays the violence and chaos **during the partition of India in 1947.
 
• The novel's focus is on how religious and social divisions **led to brutal conflicts during the partition period.**
 
 
 
• **Maila Anchal – Bhisham Sahani**
 
 
• This is **incorrect**.
 
• *Maila Anchal* (translated as *The Soiled Breeze*) was written by **Phanishwar Nath Renu**, not Bhisham Sahani.
 
• Renu is** well-known for his depiction** of rural India in his writing.
 
• ***Maila Anchal* deals** with the lives of rural communities in Bihar, capturing the simplicity, struggles, and joys of their existence.
 
• It is a significant work in Hindi literature that reflects the socio-political issues of the time.
 
 
 
• **Chitralekha – Phanishwar Nath Renu**
 
 
• This is **incorrect**.
 
• *Chitralekha* was actually written by **Ravindra Kiran** (also known as **R.K. Laxman**) and is not a work of Phanishwar Nath Renu.
 
• The novel deals with themes of love, spirituality, and the complexities of human desires.
 
• It is **set against the backdrop of ancient Indian culture** and is a philosophical exploration of human life.
